introH2: 🏭 What kinds of stays are near Amata Nakorn, Chonburi, and how do you pick the right one for your work and budget?
introHtml: Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate (now officially named Amata City Chonburi) is one of the largest estates in eastern Thailand, home to the factories and offices of many multinational companies, Japanese firms in particular. That gives people looking for a place to stay here a very different set of priorities from beachgoers — what you want is a clean room, a quick drive to your work site, easy parking, and a price you can keep within budget rather than sea views or a resort feel. The stays in this area really do come in several shapes: some are 4-star hotels with a breakfast buffet and a pool, some are condo-style serviced apartments you can rent by the month with a small kitchen in the room, some are standalone garden bungalows quiet enough to sleep soundly, and some are budget rooms just a few minutes from the estate. Plenty of people book in this area only to find the location doesn't actually match their work site, or expect a tourist-hotel atmosphere and come away disappointed. This article rounds up 5 stays near Amata Nakorn, Chonburi that we've reviewed in depth — across Khlong Tamru, Nong Mai Daeng, Na Pa, and Don Hua Lo — every one based on reading genuine guest reviews, with the upsides and the caveats laid out honestly, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: The Amata Nakorn area has no train line and public transport isn't as dense as in the city, so nearly every stay in this article is most convenient if you have your own car, and all of them have free parking. Without a car, plan to use a ride-hailing app or ask the property about its car service in advance. The zones covered in this article: Khlong Tamru — where the estate meets the town, a few minutes' drive to the Amata estate and about 15 min to Central Chonburi (Kameo, Patt) · Nong Mai Daeng — about 3 min from Amata Nakorn, walkable to Ninja Market Amata (J&Y Lodge) · Na Pa — a quiet, leafy area further in, about 8.3 km from the estate (Patoey House) · Don Hua Lo — a residential and factory zone, about 12 min by car to the estate (Bun Som) · all about 40–69 km from Suvarnabhumi Airport depending on the location.

entries.storyHtml: Among the stays in the Amata Nakorn area, if you had to pick the single most complete one that estate workers know well, many reviews give it to Kameo Hotel Amata Bangpakong — a 4-star hotel and serviced apartment by Cape & Kantary Hotels under the Kameo Collection brand, which makes value its selling point. It sits in Khlong Tamru, Mueang Chonburi, in the Amata Nakorn area, a few minutes' drive from Amata City Chonburi Industrial Estate, and scores 8.5 from 226 reviews on Trip.com. The thing guests mention most consistently is rooms that are larger than the price suggests — there are around 159 rooms and suites, from Superior with a king bed up to Studio Suite and One-Bedroom Suite that add a sitting area and a kitchenette, suited to both a single night and a month-long stay. What reviews single out for praise is the breakfast buffet that includes Japanese dishes, which fits the guests who work with Japanese companies in the estate perfectly; many say it's the reason they come back. There's an outdoor pool, gym, sauna, and steam room to unwind after work, plus free parking and a 24-hour desk that handles late check-ins. Honest caveats from the reviews: Wi-Fi caps the number of devices per room and the speed isn't always high, so anyone with online meetings should bring a backup SIM; the location is in the estate, not a tourist district, so there isn't much to walk to around the hotel and you'll need a car or a ride-hailing app; and it's a fair distance from Bang Saen beach. This isn't a stay for a beach holiday, but it's the most well-rounded option for estate workers, long-stay guests, and people driving through who want a spacious, clean room with everything included for a low four-figure budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're here for estate work or staying several nights, ask the hotel directly about weekly or monthly rates — the per-night price is usually far cheaper than booking day by day. And if you have online meetings, bring a backup SIM or pocket Wi-Fi, since there are reviews about the internet speed.

entries.storyHtml: If you mean to stay in the Amata Nakorn area for many days or many months and want a room you can actually live in like your own condo, Patt Serviced Apartments is a name worth keeping on the list — a condo-style serviced apartment on Soi Thonglor in Khlong Tamru, in the middle of the Amata Nakorn estate, about a 15-minute walk away, scoring 8.3 from 34 reviews on Trip.com. What sets it apart from many similarly priced apartments is that it has an outdoor pool and gym free to use, open 06:00–22:00 daily, so you can still go for a relaxing swim after work — and reviews note it's a saltwater pool, gentler on skin and eyes than chlorine. Most rooms are around 34 square metres, condo-style in bright tones, with a fridge, microwave, satellite TV, and safe, and some have a kitchenette with a sofa and dining nook; many have a balcony. What reviews agree on is that rooms are clean and spacious, the in-room amenities are complete for a long stay, the free parking is convenient with no scramble for a spot, and the staff look after you well. The best value is in the monthly rate, starting around ฿9,000/month for a long lease, ideal for estate workers who need to stay several months. Honest caveats from the reviews: a few mention a cigarette smell in some rooms and slow-draining bathroom pipes, so check the room's condition at check-in and report any problem right away; housekeeping sometimes knocks to clean around 8 a.m. without notice, so ask for a do-not-disturb sign if you want to sleep in; and the building is on the industrial-estate side, not by the beach, so it suits people with a car. In short, it's the best value for amenities-per-baht among serviced apartments in this area, suited to estate workers and families relocating temporarily.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you plan to stay several months, ask the property directly about the monthly rate (from about ฿9,000 for a long lease) — far better value than booking day by day. And check that the room you book has the kitchenette and bathtub you want, since the amenities differ by room type.

entries.storyHtml: Among the stays in this area, measured by sheer volume of reviews and proximity to the estate, J&Y Lodge Hotel has the most reviews in this article — about 537 on Agoda, a score of 7.6, and SHA Plus certification. It's a 3-star budget hotel that has been open since around 2012, located in Nong Mai Daeng, Mueang Chonburi. Its main draw is being only about 3 minutes by car from the Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and roughly 8 minutes from Chonburi Hospital, which makes it convenient for people commuting into the estate every day or visiting the hospital. There are 146 rooms, all around 28 sq m — roomy enough for a hotel at this price — split by bed type into Budget Twin, Deluxe Double, Deluxe Twin, and Deluxe Room. What reviews mention most is Ninja Market Amata, just about 320 metres away, where you can walk for an evening bite any day, plus free parking, free Wi-Fi, and a 24-hour front desk that handles shift workers. The caveat that has to be said plainly, from the reviews: scores differ a lot by platform — Agoda gives about 7.6 from a large sample of 537 reviews, while Booking.com gives only about 5.6 from a small sample of just 6, which suggests the experience may be inconsistent, so read recent reviews from several sources before booking. The building has been open since around 2012, so some spots are starting to show their age and upkeep isn't uniform across every room; if you get a room not in the condition you expected, ask the front desk to switch right away. There's no pool here, and getting around is easiest with a car. It suits estate workers and overnight stopovers focused mainly on a location close to the estate and a budget price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Scores differ a lot by platform (Agoda ~7.6 · Booking ~5.6) — read recent reviews from several sources before booking, and tell the front desk right away if a room isn't as expected so you can switch. Have about ฿500 ready for the deposit at check-in, refunded when you check out.

entries.type: 2.5-Star Bungalow Guesthouse · Quiet, in a garden
entries.name: Patoey House
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Pa · ~8.3 km from Amata Nakorn estate
entries.storyHtml: If the other estate-area stays in this article are blocks of rooms in a row, Patoey House sells the opposite — standalone bungalow rooms set in a garden, quiet, with private parking right by your door. It's a 2.5-star bungalow-style guesthouse at Moo 11, Na Pa, Mueang Chonburi, in the quiet, leafy inner part of Na Pa, about 8.3 kilometres from the Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, scoring 8.7 from 5 reviews on Trip.com with a cleanliness score as high as 9.3. What guests agree on is that the rooms are very clean, the atmosphere is quiet and shady like a garden home, the beds are comfortable, and there's private parking by your door with no scramble for a spot — the main reason people who drive themselves choose it. There are several room types to suit your budget and group size, from a single-bed room, a queen room, and a deluxe king room to a twin-bed room for families, all in the form of standalone bungalows that are more private than rooms inside a building. A highlight rare at this price is that it's pet-friendly, ideal for those who don't want to leave the dog or cat at home, plus free Wi-Fi, CCTV, and an alarm system in the common areas. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no pool and no breakfast; a few reviews mention a smell from the bathroom drain in some rooms, fixed by closing the bathroom door when not in use; the desk keeps set hours (about 9:00 a.m. to midnight), so let them know your check-in time in advance if you arrive late; some payments are cash only; and it's a newer stay with not many reviews yet, so read the most recent ones too. It suits estate workers who want a quiet stay, self-drivers, travellers stopping over en route, and people bringing a pet along.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The desk keeps set hours (about 9:00 a.m. to midnight), so if you arrive late or off-hours, contact the property in advance to arrange a hand-off. Carry some cash, since some payments are cash only, and if you're bringing a pet, let them know and ask about the conditions before booking.

entries.storyHtml: We close with the smallest, most budget-friendly option in the article, Bun Som Apartment — a small apartment of about 5 rooms on Wiboon Pracharak Rd in Don Hua Lo, Mueang Chonburi, in a residential and factory zone, about a 12-minute drive to the Amata Nakorn estate. To be upfront from the start, this is a property that has only just entered the booking system, so it has no accumulated review score on the platforms yet — its status is still "awaiting reviews." The information in our review is therefore based mainly on the nature of the property and the context of the similar Don Hua Lo–Amata Nakorn area. What makes it appealing to a certain group is the quiet air-con rooms with a fridge, a flat-screen TV, a work desk, free drinking water, and free on-site parking with no scramble for a spot, suited to estate workers, tradespeople or contractor teams in for several days, and budget long-stay guests who drive themselves. The in-room fridge makes it easy to buy food to keep or reheat when you get back late, plus there's a laundry service that helps with a long stay. It takes both daily and monthly bookings, from about ฿650/night, with the monthly rate far better value than booking day by day for long stays. Caveats to know before booking: there's no pool, no gym, and no breakfast; it's a small property whose desk keeps set hours (about 08:00–22:00), not 24 hours; it takes mainly cash; and there are no accumulated reviews to go on, so we recommend calling for details and asking to see photos of the actual room directly at 081 567 7443 before booking. It suits factory workers and tradespeople who just need a clean, quiet air-con room close to work and a low budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Since this is a small property of about 5 rooms with no accumulated reviews, call to check availability and ask for details directly at 081 567 7443 before booking. For a long stay, ask about the monthly rate, which is far better value, and have cash ready since it takes mainly cash.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common questions travellers ask about stays near Amata Nakorn, Chonburi

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best stay near Amata Nakorn, Chonburi?
faq.a: It depends on your work and budget. If you want the most complete pick with breakfast and a pool, Kameo Hotel Amata Bangpakong, a 4-star hotel by Cape & Kantary scoring 8.5, is the answer. For a long monthly stay with a condo room and a pool, Patt Serviced Apartments. To be as close to the estate as possible on a budget, J&Y Lodge Hotel is only 3 min away and has the most reviews, 537. For a quiet private room where you can bring a pet, Patoey House. And on a tight budget for factory work, Bun Som Apartment.

faq.q: ❓ How much do stays near Amata Nakorn cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿490–1,200 per night. The most budget-friendly is Patoey House from ฿490 · J&Y Lodge and Bun Som from ฿650 · Patt from ฿720 · and the 4-star hotel level is Kameo from ฿1,200. Serviced apartments and apartments like Patt, Kameo, and Bun Som have monthly rates that are far better value than booking day by day for estate workers staying long — ask the property directly.

faq.q: ❓ Can you stay by the month in the Amata Nakorn area?
faq.a: Yes, at several places. Patt Serviced Apartments has a monthly rate from about ฿9,000/month for a long lease, and some condo-style rooms have a kitchenette. Kameo Hotel handles long stays with Studio/One-Bedroom Suite rooms that have a kitchenette — ask about the monthly rate. Bun Som Apartment also takes monthly on a budget. All usually get a lower per-night price when you book monthly directly with the property, ideal for estate workers staying several weeks to several months.

faq.q: ❓ Are stays near Amata Nakorn convenient without a car?
faq.a: To be honest, the Amata Nakorn area is most convenient with your own car, since public transport isn't as dense as in the city, and every stay in the article has free parking. Without a car, J&Y Lodge has the edge because it's a walk to Ninja Market Amata (~320 m) and has a taxi-calling service. For the others, plan to use a ride-hailing app or ask the property about its car service in advance, especially Patoey House and Bun Som, which are on lanes in the Na Pa–Don Hua Lo area where rides aren't as frequent as in the city.

faq.q: ❓ Which stays in the Amata Nakorn area have a pool?
faq.a: Two stays in this article have a pool. Kameo Hotel Amata Bangpakong has an outdoor pool, gym, sauna, and steam room. Patt Serviced Apartments has an outdoor pool (reviews say it's saltwater) and a free gym, open 06:00–22:00 daily. J&Y Lodge, Patoey House, and Bun Som have no pool, keeping things simple and budget-friendly — if a pool is a must, choose the first two.

faq.q: ❓ How far in advance should you book a stay in the Amata Nakorn area?
faq.a: Usually 1–2 weeks is enough, but during trade shows or events in the Amata Nakorn estate, rooms tend to fill up fast and prices rise, so book several weeks ahead — especially J&Y Lodge and Kameo, the larger stays that estate workers book heavily. Every platform usually has Free Cancellation; we recommend locking in a price that way first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best rate. For Patt and Bun Som, which take monthly, ask the property directly to check availability and the long-stay rate.
